primary_claim: Across independent North American and Australian acoustic monitoring systems, more recent rainfall is associated with greater short-window overlap in frog calling activity across species.
interpretation: shared environmental activation is consistent with transient compression of temporal separation among calling species

FrogID.design: expert-validated short call recordings conditional on >=1 calling species

temperature.interpretation_authorized: warmer conditions are associated with greater event-level multispecies calling overlap in NAAMP after plausibility QC and flexible day-of-year adjustment

prohibited: direct meta-analysis of NAAMP and FrogID odds ratios
first-ever rainfall effect on frog calling or species richness
